display.title: The Precious Gift of Time: The Boy Who Lost His Dollar
display.summary_short: We cannot control time, only what we fill it with. A boy who keeps wishing for the dollar he lost shows why wasted time never comes back.
display.summary_long: A talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show during Sefiras HaOmer. Counting the Omer means counting time, one of Hashem's most precious gifts. Uncle Yossi asks why we count something we cannot control: we cannot slow time down, speed it up or stop it, but we can choose what we put into it, wisely or foolishly, and time that is lost never comes back. He tells of a boy named Avraham who loses the birthday dollar his father gave him. His father kindly gives him another, then another, but each time the boy says that with the first dollar he would have one more, until his father explains that he must forget what is lost and take good care of what he has. So too with time: set aside time each day to daven, learn Torah, help your parents and help your friends, and Hashem will bless you with long and good years.
display.lesson: Time is a precious gift from Hashem; use every day wisely for davening, Torah and helping others, because lost time never comes back.

characters: Avraham, a boy who lost his dollar
